source_edition.title: The Holy Sacrifice of the Mass

identified_disputes.statement: Guéranger parses sanctum sacrificium, immaculatam hostiam as identifying Eucharistic offering accepted by God; a later reproduction attributes to Gihr p.660 n.1 a different grammatical analysis that attaches the phrase to Melchisedech's offering.
identified_disputes.educational_policy: Present both as distinct historical interpretations, explicitly label secondary mediation of Gihr, never state either as universally settled grammar.

identified_disputes.statement: Gihr p.627 is cited by Foley (2025) in support of 'in every respect' rather than merely 'in all things'; exact original page still needs inspection.
A hypothetical heaven-sent fire over Abel's offering is not present in Genesis 4. If present in Gihr, it must be identified as interpretive speculation, not Scripture.

claims.author: Dom Prosper Guéranger
claims.locator: SUPRA QUAE
claims.editorial_observation: Guéranger reads sanctum sacrificium and immaculatam hostiam as receiving the Eucharistic offering; this is in explicit conflict with the later secondary report of Gihr's grammatical footnote. Guéranger's attribution of the phrase to Leo I is a historical claim requiring independent source corroboration.

claims.author: Fr Nicholas Gihr
claims.editorial_observation: P0 warns that the hypothesis of heavenly fire marking Abel's accepted offering is absent from Genesis. Must classify as Gihr's interpretative hypothesis, never an explicit biblical statement. Printed p. 659 unavailable for direct checking.

claims.author: Fr Nicholas Gihr
claims.editorial_observation: Secondary 2016 account reproduces Gihr's distinction between intrinsic acceptance of Christ's sacrifice and the devotion of those offering, but the original p. 659 is not independently collated.

claims.author: Fr Nicholas Gihr
claims.locator: §61 p. 660; earlier discussion pp. 75–76
claims.editorial_observation: May 2005 Sancta Liturgia attributes to Gihr p. 660 footnote 1 the grammatical reading that sanctum sacrificium, immaculatam hostiam modifies the Melchisedech offering. Guéranger's independent published interpretation takes the opposite view. Original Gihr footnote must be checked; record interpretative disagreement without automatic resolution.
